claim: The formation of amyloid bodies is seeded by non-coding RNA transcribed from loci of the rDNA intergenic spacer (rIGSRNA) and likely driven by complex coacervation of low-complexity rIGSRNA and short cationic domains in amyloid converting motif (ACM).
source: The formation of amyloid bodies is seeded by non-coding RNA transcribed from loci of the rDNA intergenic spacer (rIGSRNA) and likely driven by complex coacervation of low-complexity rIGSRNA and short cationic domains in amyloid converting motif (ACM) (Wang et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2018b.

claim: Acidosis stress as found in tumor microenvironments induces the assembly of amyloid bodies, which involves the recruitment of many proteins involved in cell cycle regulation and DNA synthesis to amyloid bodies.
source: Acidosis stress as found in tumor microenvironments was shown to induce the assembly of amyloid bodies, which involved the recruitment of many proteins involved in cell cycle regulation and DNA synthesis to amyloid bodies (Audas et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Audas et al., 2016.

claim: Amyloid body formation induces a protective state of cellular dormancy that may help cancer cells to adapt to the harsh tumor microenvironment.
source: It was postulated that amyloid body formation induces a protective state of cellular dormancy that may help cancer cells to adapt to the harsh tumor microenvironment (Wang et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Wang et al., 2019 and involves speculation.

claim: Inhibition of amyloid body formation by knockdown of rIGS28RNA prevented tumor dormancy and led to larger tumor sizes in cancer mouse models.
source: In agreement with this, inhibition of amyloid body formation by knockdown of rIGS28RNA prevented tumor dormancy and led to larger tumor sizes in cancer mouse models (Audas et al., 2016; Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Audas et al., 2016 and illustrated in Figure 6.

claim: Condensates have been implicated in almost all fundamental processes in living cells.
source: Condensates have now been implicated in almost all fundamental processes in living cells.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the breadth of condensate research.

claim: Condensate research will make an important contribution to unraveling the complex biology of cancers in the coming years.
source: Given the importance of condensates for cellular physiology and our increasingly better understanding of condensate assembly and function, we expect that condensate research will make an important contribution to unraveling the complex biology of cancers in the coming years.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future research directions.

claim: Assembly of transcription factors into aberrant condensates could drive various hallmarks of cancer cells.
source: One example of the increasingly important role of condensates is the demonstration that transcription is regulated by condensates. Numerous cancer-related proteins function as transcription factors and assembly of these transcription factors into aberrant condensates could drive various hallmarks of cancer cells, such as their ability to proliferate.
evidence: This is inferred from the role of condensates in transcription and the involvement of transcription factors in cancer.

claim: Cancer cells acquire capabilities such as induction of angiogenesis, activation of invasion and metastasis, deregulation of cellular energetics, avoidance of immune detection, and destabilization of the genome during tumorigenesis.
source: However, cancer cells acquire various other capabilities during tumorigenesis, such as induction of angiogenesis, activation of invasion and metastasis, deregulation of cellular energetics, avoidance of immune detection, and destabilization of the genome (Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hanahan and Weinberg, 2011.

claim: Condensates have confirmed roles in mitosis, immune cell signal transduction, chromatin organization, and cell adhesion.
source: Increasing evidence implicates condensates also in these processes, with confirmed roles for example in mitosis (Jiang et al., 2015; Rai et al., 2018), immune cell signal transduction (Su et al., 2016), chromatin organization (Gibson et al., 2019), and cell adhesion (Beutel et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jiang et al., 2015; Rai et al., 2018; Su et al., 2016; Gibson et al., 2019; Beutel et al., 2019.

claim: The growing field of condensate biology will create more knowledge about the molecular underpinnings of cancer and accelerate the development of new therapies.
source: We expect that the growing field of condensate biology will not only create more knowledge about the molecular underpinnings of cancer but it will also accelerate the development of new therapies, thus bringing us closer to the goal of curing cancer.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the future impact of condensate research.
